headline: Google DeepMind says a new AI system has designed two enzymes that nature never made, one of which makes a drug ingredient 99 times faster than today's industrial method.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: DeepMind's own preprint results, relayed by one secondary outlet with no second source or DeepMind page found, and nothing peer reviewed.
importance_line: If the results hold, the enzymes could in time help cut the cost of making drug ingredients and break down a plastic softener found in food packaging and medical tubing, but the figures are DeepMind's own, come from a preprint that is not peer reviewed, and are relayed by one outlet.
summary: Startup Fortune reports that Google DeepMind has released a preprint (a paper not yet reviewed by outside experts), announced on X on 5 Oct 2026 by vice president Pushmeet Kohli, for AlphaProtein Novo, an AI system that designs enzymes (proteins that speed up chemical reactions) from scratch rather than adjusting natural ones. DeepMind says its two test enzymes are one that makes piperidine, a building block of many drugs, 99 times faster than the current industrial process and one that breaks down DEHP, a plastic softener that regulators have flagged for links to reproductive harm and liver damage; outside collaborators included a group at the Francis Crick Institute.
notes: Read in full. Single source: Google News searches on 6 Oct 2026 found no other outlet and no DeepMind page for AlphaProtein Novo, so the figures could not be cross-checked; score lowered by one for that. The page also holds unrelated link teasers, ignored. Pushmeet Kohli also fronted DeepMind's SynthID Bio announcement of 30 Sep 2026 (item C04-04); the two are separate stories.
